column3: It closely parallels water sent into the earth and producing varied crops, extending the focus's directed renewal.
Its repeated blindness supplies a limited counterpart to the focus's final call for insight.
The reproductive-water scene does not clarify water driven to barren land for crop production.
The reduction of land offers only a distant counterpoint to the focus's restoration of barren ground.
The preceding ayah also asks whether people will perceive an evident sign, framing the focus's closing question.
It establishes earth as prepared for living creatures, a background for the focus's revived ground and provision.
Water is made the basis of all living things and the same observational challenge is pressed on deniers.
Human creation from clay does not develop the focus's water, crop, or perception sequence.
Its command to examine creation for flaws gives a broad but nonspecific parallel to attentive seeing.
Created livestock under human use helps illuminate the focus's crop as food for herds as well as people.
It joins made-habitable earth, descending water, and vegetation brought forth in a close parallel sequence.
Rain sent down and made drinkable shows water as a divinely directed life-giving provision, without the barren-land scene.
Its appeal to recognize a visible divine favor only broadly resembles the focus's appeal to see.
Leadership, patience, and certainty do not clarify the ecological sign in the focus.
Its barren ground is the explicit opposite state from which the focus's driven water draws a crop.
It asks people to look at the earth's abundant noble growth, directly reinforcing the focus's evidentiary vegetation.
Human eating and livestock grazing directly echo the two recipients of the focus's crop.
Bringing a people from darkness to light is a distinct metaphorical movement, not the focus's material renewal.
It traces descending water through vegetation and grain, closely expanding the focus's crop brought forth by water.
Seeing people ally with disbelievers does not illuminate the focus's ecological or perceptual sign.
The emphatic pouring of water supplies the incoming provision that the focus depicts as driven to the land.
One water irrigates adjoining lands and yields differentiated crops and food, closely clarifying productive water.
Its failed attempt to come out of the Fire is only a remote contrast to beneficial bringing forth.
Abundantly poured water supports the focus's portrayal of water as a supplied life-giving input.
Day made seeing offers a general condition of visibility, but not the focus's sign of renewed land.
Water and pasture are brought out from the earth, directly connecting land's yield to animal provision.
The crop image conveys gradual growth, but functions as a social parable rather than ecological evidence.
Water is driven to dead land and brings out fruit, then explicitly serves as a sign of resurrection.
The return at death does not clarify the focus's water-driven agricultural renewal.
The threat of inaccessible water exposes dependence on the resource that the focus shows being directed and supplied.
Looking without seeing is a direct negative counterpart to the focus's final demand for true perception.
Eating food and being shown signs give only a limited background for provision becoming evidence.
The invitation to observe upheld birds supports attentive observation, but concerns a different sign.
The imperative to look broadly echoes the focus's demand to see without sharing its scene.
The giving of Moses's Book and guidance does not clarify the focus's ecological sign.
It distinguishes human sowing from the divine act of growing, directly sharpening the focus's "We bring forth" claim.
Seeing a future outcome is only a general parallel to the focus's call for perception.
Provision is explicitly for humans and their livestock, matching the two consumers named in the focus.
Divine all-seeing provides a broad theological parallel, not the focus's observed renewal.
The she-camel's eating on God's land loosely relates animal sustenance to the land's provision.
Hidden delight for the righteous does not develop the focus's visible sign in earth and crop.
The final driving toward the Lord is a different movement from water driven to land.
Its inability to hear or see offers a general negative counterpart to the focus's perceptual rebuke.
God's knowledge of eyes and hearts is distinct from the audience's requested observation.
The bodily image of legs intertwined does not clarify the focus.
Its comparison of unbelievers' eating to livestock gives a limited contrast to the focus's shared provision for both.
Punishment for denying the meeting does not clarify the agricultural sign.
Unseen divine support provides only a remote contrast to the focus's visible evidence.
Eating through Solomon's staff does not illuminate crop production or insight.
The principle that a favor changes with people's inner change is only a distant framework for received provision.
Driving criminals to Hell reverses the verb's setting and does not clarify water driven to land.
It directly pairs water on lifeless earth with stirring, growth, and plants as evidence for resurrection.
Provision received and spent offers a limited connection to the focus's provision for people.
Measured rain revives a dead town and explicitly analogizes that renewal to being brought forth.
Its invitation to examine created beings broadly supports observation but not the focus's particular sign.
Speech discipline and diseased desire do not clarify the focus.
Waiting for someone to come out is unrelated to water bringing crop from barren earth.
Gardens, palms, and crops present land as a productive provision, though without the focus's water-driven renewal.
The immediately preceding lesser punishment is another sign meant to turn people back, contrasting with the focus's sustaining sign.
The heart's truthful seeing supports the focus's movement from visible phenomenon to inward recognition.
The dream of pressing wine and birds eating bread does not clarify the focus's scene.
Earth's spread prepares the setting from which the following water and pasture are brought out.
The question about drinking water highlights human dependence on water supplied beyond their control.
Eyes, hearts, and ears left unused directly clarify the focus's rebuke of those who will not see.
Sight and hearts are given faculties whose neglected gratitude parallels the focus's call to use sight rightly.
The earth's spreading is only a general background for its later productive capacity.
Water issuing from rock gives a limited parallel to life-supporting water emerging in relation to hardened perception.
Day made seeing supports visibility in general but not the focus's specific ecological sign.
Abundant rain and running rivers show environmental provision, though the ayah's point is a destroyed community.
Denying divine signs offers a general counterpart to refusing the focus's visible sign.
It shows the fitting response to divine signs, complementing the focus's question about whether people will see.
The removal of believers from a condemned town is unrelated to agricultural bringing forth.
Striving with possessions and selves does not clarify the focus's provision or perception.
The statement of loss does not illuminate the focus's sequence.
Sweet water given to drink supplies a concrete form of the life-sustaining water in the focus.
Migration and striving with possessions and selves do not clarify the focus.
The command's descent from heaven to earth gives a broad directional framework, without water or crop renewal.
Seeing one's smallest evil deed is unrelated to the focus's ecological sign.
Its call to reason after passing a sign broadly resembles the focus's appeal to perceive.
Creation of heavens and earth and the call to remember offer only a broad framework for the focus's sign.
Descending water makes earth green, a concise direct parallel to the focus's restored barren land.
The conduct of believers in striving does not clarify the focus.
Water reaches humbled earth, which stirs, swells, and lives, explicitly grounding resurrection in observed renewal.
The call to remember is a general response to evidence, without the focus's scene.
Signs in the earth broadly include the focus's phenomenon but add no specific clarification.
The protected she-camel eating on God's land loosely echoes animal sustenance, without the crop-and-water sequence.
Deliverance from darkness to light is metaphorical and does not clarify ecological renewal.
God seeing what people do is only a distant parallel to the focus's call for human sight.
The moderated climate of Paradise does not clarify water, crops, or the focus's perceptual rebuke.
Concealing disclosed information and the appeal to reason do not illuminate the focus.
A ruined town, preserved food, and restored bones make resurrection observable, though without the focus's water-to-crop sequence.
Rules against expelling divorced women use a different sense of bringing out.
The return to God and the fate of transgressors do not clarify the focus.
Forcing the Prophet from the land uses a different sense of removal.
Divine nearness and knowledge of inner whispering do not clarify the focus.
Looking without seeing directly explains why the focus's final question demands more than physical sight.
Its rhetorical call to fear God only broadly resembles the focus's rhetorical rebuke.
Provision is sent down in measured amount with full knowledge, supporting the focus's portrayal of directed sustenance.
Hypocrisy, repentance, and punishment do not clarify the focus's scene.
Its question about recognizing denial through conduct supports the focus's use of a question to demand discerning sight.
It joins made-habitable earth, descending water, and fruits provided for people in a close foundational parallel.
Rain revives dead earth, disperses creatures, and is presented among signs for people who reason.
Its cultivated and uncultivated gardens, crops, and harvest establish land's yield as provision, though water is not named.
Good land yields vegetation by its Lord's permission while bad land yields scant growth, directly sharpening the focus's barren-land contrast.
Water descends, earth's plants grow into food for people and livestock, and the scene exposes the fragility of terrestrial abundance.
Rain sent from heaven and added strength portray renewed provision, without the focus's explicit crop sequence.
Spread earth, rivers, and paired fruits provide a broad environmental setting for the focus's productive land.
Water sent from heaven runs through valleys according to measure, clarifying directed and apportioned water without crop production.
Water is sent down to bring forth fruits as provision, directly paralleling the focus's causal sequence.
The spread earth contains weighed growth and provision, supplying the productive-land background of the focus.
Rain gives both drink and pasture for grazing, directly linking water with livestock provision.
The same rain grows crops, olives, palms, grapes, and every fruit, closely expanding the focus's crop brought forth.
Water revives earth after its death and is explicitly presented as a sign for those who listen.
Rain-fed vegetation grows and then becomes scattered dry matter, supplying the focus's living crop with its temporal counterpoint.
Water is sent down in due measure and lodged in the earth, clarifying controlled delivery and storage before growth.
Purifying water is sent down from the sky, supplying the same divinely directed water movement as the focus.
The water revives dead land and is given as drink to cattle and many people, nearly repeating the focus's recipients and renewal.
Water from heaven produces delightful gardens whose trees people cannot cause to grow, directly supporting the focus's divine "We bring forth."
Water sent from heaven revives earth after death, and the response is praise to God.
Rain and earth's revival after death are explicitly named signs, matching the focus's evidentiary logic.
Water from heaven brings forth noble paired growth, closely paralleling crop production from supplied water.
Winds drive cloud to dead land, which is revived by rain; the verse explicitly connects this process to resurrection.
Dead land is revived and grain brought out from it for people to eat, a direct counterpart to the focus's crop from barren land.
Gardens with palms, vines, and springs extend the focus's crop into a sustained food-bearing landscape.
Water sent from heaven gives provision and is one of God's signs, though its agricultural sequence remains implicit.
Rain is sent after despair and mercy spread, giving the focus's directed provision a clear restoration setting.
Water sent down revives earth after death and is listed as a sign for people who understand.
Blessed water brings forth gardens, grain, and palms, directly elaborating the focus's water-to-crop movement.
The water gives life to dead land, and this renewal is explicitly made an analogy for coming forth.
The command to know that God gives life to earth after its death directly states the focus's underlying sign.
Abundant rain from heaven depicts water as a renewed divine gift, without the focus's crop detail.
Rain is followed by gardens and rivers, extending provision into an enduring fertile landscape.
Abundant water is sent down from rain clouds, supplying the focus's incoming life-giving source.
The water brings forth grain and vegetation, closely matching the focus's crop drawn from supplied water.
Lush gardens complete the water-to-vegetation sequence with a fertile outcome.
The earth is split open after the preceding pouring of water, providing the focus's transition from water to emergence.
Grain is caused to grow from the opened earth, directly paralleling the focus's crop brought forth.
Grapes and fodder extend the produced crop into food for people and animals.
Olives and palms elaborate the productive vegetation that follows supplied water.
Dense gardens extend the focus's crop outcome into cultivated abundance.
Fruit and pasture directly correspond to the focus's provision for human selves and livestock.
It explicitly identifies the preceding produce as enjoyment for people and their livestock, matching the focus's final clause.
Bringing forth pasture provides a concise parallel to the focus's vegetation as animal provision.
Two gardens and the command to eat the Lord's provision portray fertile land as a visible sign requiring gratitude.
The replacement of fruitful gardens with bitter and sparse growth supplies a direct negative counterpoint to restored fertility.
Earth is made traversable so people may eat its provision, clarifying the focus's crop as divinely available sustenance.
